Seven years ago, on Aug. 10, 2019, Jeffrey Epstein was found
[dead](https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/26/politics/epstein-files-prison-officials-
night-he-died) inside his cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in
Manhattan while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges. New York
City's medical examiner
[ruled](https://www.npr.org/2019/08/16/751869191/jeffrey-epsteins-death-ruled-
a-suicide-by-new-york-medical-examiner) his death a suicide by hanging, later
supported by [federal
investigations.](https://oig.justice.gov/sites/default/files/reports/23-085.pdf)

But the staggering [failures](https://oig.justice.gov/news/doj-oig-releases-
report-bops-custody-care-and-supervision-jeffrey-epstein-metropolitan), from
guards who neglected to conduct required checks to falsified records to
malfunctioning security cameras, have maintained the air of suspicion and
conspiracy that still [surrounds](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-
news/jeffrey-epstein-unanswered-questions-final-hours-orange-flash-search-
rcna264147) his death.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

In the years just before and since Epstein's death, several figures in his
orbit have died, including former business partners, employees, alleged
associates, and survivors. They've died under circumstances varying from
cancer to suicide, overdose, and, in one recent case, a cause that has yet to
be determined. Like Epstein himself, they took with them firsthand knowledge
of his world, answers to questions we may never get.
